what_happened: Diagnosed task-lock.sh's cmd_acquire_retry as counter-based (never reads the clock), explaining instance B's load-sensitive elapsed-time measurements; designed and sandbox-validated a PATH-shimmed fake-sleep causal fix (sleep_count == BUDGET_MS/POLL_MS) requiring zero production-code changes, verified against two different budget values.

test-detect-noop-bash.sh failed on a pre-existing, two-day-stale, untracked, empty directory at agent-system/extensions/core/tmp (not created by the suite's own code, which unconditionally sets NOOP_BASH_STATE_DIR). Removed the empty dir (fixed, suite now 50/0); the same failure recurred transiently during a full-corpus run and was gone again afterward, consistent with external interference from a concurrent process on this shared host -- root cause not fully pinned. Recommended a delta-based (before/after) fix for the implement phase rather than the current absolute-existence check.

Full 153-suite run-all.sh surfaced two reproducible-in-isolation real defects unrelated to the ambient-host-state axes this task owns: test-guard-git-push.sh's expired-grant case (likely a grant-matching/test-isolation bug, not a timing-window issue -- PG_EXPIRY_WINDOW=600s vs test's 700s age has 100s of slack) and test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh's eager-load byte-count drift (67088 vs baseline 66100). Both flagged for separate owners per the dispatch's instruction not to misfile unrelated defect classes into this task's triage.
